patients.summary: Retired math teacher with Parkinson disease since 2016, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, BPH and diverticulosis who joins in 2018. Over the following years he has two diverticular bleeds, dopamine-agonist psychosis, an NSTEMI and an inferior STEMI with two stents, and a left central retinal artery occlusion.

Records received by fax ahead of new patient appointment 10/2. 31 pages: last two office notes, med list, problem list, labs from 2017 and spring 2018, colonoscopy report 2016, urology summary 2017, neurology letter 4/2018. Scanned to chart, flagged for PCP review.

PCP review summary:
- Parkinson disease dx 2016 by outside neurology, still followed there. Sinemet 25/100 TID, rasagiline 1 mg qAM.
- HTN on lisinopril 20 and metoprolol succinate 50, controlled on their readings.
- Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40.
- BPH with LUTS on tamsulosin 0.4 qhs. Diagnostic cystoscopy 3/2017 (outside urology): enlarged prostate, no bladder lesion.
- Screening colonoscopy 4/2016: no polyps, sigmoid diverticulosis. Prep good.
- ASA 81 daily, primary prevention per prior PCP.
- NKDA. Never smoker.
- Prior labs unremarkable.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65 y/o retired high school math teacher transferring care. Wanted a practice where he could reach his doctor directly. Here with his wife.

PD diagnosed 2016, followed by outside neurology, last seen spring. Tremor R>L, slower than he used to be, still does everything himself. On Sinemet TID and rasagiline, no side effects he can name. Takes doses on time, wife keeps a pill box.

HTN: on lisinopril 20 + metoprolol succ 50 for years. Home cuff readings 120s/70s. No CP, no SOB, no palpitations, no edema.
Lipids: atorvastatin 40, no muscle aches.
BPH: on tamsulosin, urology workup 2017 incl cystoscopy. Says stream is fine for now, up once a night.
Diverticulosis on 2016 colonoscopy. No bleeding, no abd pain, bowels regular.
ASA 81 daily, started by prior PCP.

Meds: carbidopa-levodopa 25-100 TID, rasagiline 1 mg qAM, lisinopril 20 daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, ASA 81 daily, tamsulosin 0.4 qhs.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: colonoscopy 2016, cystoscopy 2017.
FH: father MI at 72. Mother ischemic stroke at 78. One older brother with HTN. Nobody with Parkinson's or psychiatric illness.
SH: married, lives with wife in Granby. Taught HS math 30+ years, retired. Never smoked. Glass of wine once or twice a month. Walks most days.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well appearing, mild hypomimia. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT. Ext no edema. Neuro: resting tremor R hand, mild bradykinesia, gait steady with reduced arm swing R. Mood euthymic.

A/P:
1. Parkinson disease - per neurology, continue current regimen.
2. HTN - at goal, continue.
3. Hyperlipidemia - lipid panel today, continue atorvastatin.
4. BPH - stable on tamsulosin.
5. Diverticulosis - no issues.
6. HM: flu shot today (high dose). HCV and HIV screen today. Colonoscopy 2016 normal apart from diverticula. Tdap and Shingrix at Welcome to Medicare visit in the spring. PHQ-2 0.
Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, TSH, HCV, HIV.
RTC 5-6 months for Welcome to Medicare exam.

events.reason: Weakening urinary stream, nocturia, incomplete emptying

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Roger Desrosiers, 67, for lower urinary tract symptoms. He was evaluated by a urologist in 2017, including a diagnostic cystoscopy that showed an enlarged prostate and no bladder lesion, and has been on tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime since.

Over the past several months his stream has slowly weakened. He gets up at night to void and finishes with the sense that his bladder is not empty. He has had no dysuria, no gross hematuria and no urinary infections.

Other history: Parkinson disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diverticulosis. Medications: carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, aspirin 81 mg, tamsulosin. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol of note.

Exam: vital signs normal. Abdomen soft and non-distended, bladder not palpable. DRE: prostate symmetrically enlarged, smooth, non-tender, no nodules.

Data: urinalysis negative. Creatinine unchanged from his prior values. PSA 4.3, slightly above the laboratory's standard cutoff but within the expected range for his age and gland size.

Impression: symptomatic BPH with recurrent symptoms on alpha blockade.

Plan: add finasteride 5 mg daily to shrink the gland over the next 6-12 months; continue tamsulosin. Counseled that finasteride lowers PSA by roughly half, so future values should be read with that in mind. Follow-up here in six months with a repeat PSA.

Sincerely,
Urology

events.reason: Painless bright red blood per rectum with clots

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 07/04/2021. Received 07/07/2021.

CC: rectal bleeding.

HPI: 67M with known diverticulosis and BPH (urology visit in January) woke feeling normal, had breakfast, then had sudden urgency and passed a large amount of red blood with small clots. No abdominal pain. No lightheadedness. No fever. Bowel habits unchanged. Never had this before.

PMH: Parkinson disease, HTN, hyperlipidemia, BPH, diverticulosis, occasional constipation.
Meds: carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, aspirin 81, tamsulosin, finasteride.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol, lives with his wife, independent.

Vitals on arrival: T 36.9, BP 124/76, HR 88, RR 14.
Exam: alert, comfortable. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, not distended, no tenderness, guarding or mass. Rectal: bright red blood in the vault, no mass, no fissure.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, MCV 90, plt 230. PT/INR normal. BMP within normal limits.

ED course: two large-bore IVs, crystalloid. Remained hemodynamically stable. GI consulted, bowel prep started for urgent colonoscopy. Admitted to medicine.

Impression: acute painless hematochezia, presumed diverticular.

Emergency medicine attending

reports.text: Indication: acute hematochezia. Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: rapid purge, fair. Scope advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve. Fresh blood and clots in the sigmoid colon. Scattered sigmoid diverticula. One sigmoid diverticulum with active oozing at its neck; 4 mL dilute epinephrine injected around it, then bipolar cautery applied with hemostasis. Observed for several minutes without further bleeding. Remaining colon to the cecum without blood after washing; no polyps or masses. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
reports.conclusion: Bleeding sigmoid diverticulum, treated with epinephrine injection and cautery with hemostasis. Sigmoid diverticulosis. No polyps.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admission 07/04/2021 - Discharge 07/06/2021. Received 07/07/2021.

Admitting diagnosis: hematochezia.
Discharge diagnosis: diverticular hemorrhage, sigmoid colon, treated endoscopically.

Hospital course: 67M with Parkinson disease, HTN, hyperlipidemia, BPH and known diverticulosis admitted from the ED with painless hematochezia. Hemodynamically stable throughout on IV fluids. Colonoscopy the evening of admission, within 12 hours of arrival, found a bleeding sigmoid diverticulum, treated with epinephrine injection and cautery with good hemostasis. No further bleeding after the procedure. No transfusion needed. Aspirin held during admission; resumed at discharge. Diet advanced without issue.

Discharge medications: unchanged home medications, carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, rasagiline 1 mg qAM, lisinopril 20 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs, finasteride 5 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week with CBC. Return for recurrent bleeding, dizziness or black stools.

Hospital medicine

documents.title: Question about something Roger is seeing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is his wife writing on his account. For a few weeks now Roger has been telling me he sees small animals running across the living room floor, like mice or a cat. There is nothing there. He isn't upset by it and knows they aren't real once he looks closer. He's otherwise himself. Is this something to worry about? His neurology appointment is April 4.

documents.title: RE: Question about something Roger is seeing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me. Visual hallucinations like this can happen with Parkinson disease and sometimes with its medicines, so neurology is the right place for it. Please keep the April 4 appointment and tell them exactly what you told me. If he becomes confused, frightened, feverish, or the visions change suddenly, call me the same day. I'll send a note to his neurologist ahead of the visit.

medications.reason: Psychosis on dopamine agonist; taper off over two weeks

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Movement disorders clinic

Dear Doctor,

I saw Roger Desrosiers, 69, today with his wife, about nine months after our April visit for visual hallucinations. Thank you for your call in December.

His wife reports two months of visual hallucinations and paranoid thinking. He again sees small animals in the house, which she confirms are not there, and he has become suspicious of the neighbors, accusing them of taking things from him with nothing to support it. These began after pramipexole was added in October, three months ago. He takes carbidopa-levodopa, pramipexole, atorvastatin and metoprolol among his medicines. He has never had psychiatric illness.

BP 130/80, HR 68, afebrile.
Exam: rest tremor, bradykinesia and rigidity as before. No signs of infection or a metabolic cause on exam. MMSE 26/30, points lost on attention and calculation.

Assessment: psychosis induced by dopaminergic therapy, specifically the dopamine agonist, in a patient with Parkinson disease psychosis and mild cognitive impairment.

Plan:
1. Taper pramipexole off over two weeks: 0.125 mg three times daily for one week, then 0.125 mg twice daily for one week, then stop.
2. Continue carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily and rasagiline 1 mg daily.
3. Wife to call us if symptoms worsen during the taper. Follow-up in two months.

Movement disorders neurologist

- nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 07/06/2025. Received 07/10/2025.

CC: rectal bleeding.

HPI: 71M with diverticulosis, on aspirin, with a prior painless diverticular bleed in 2021, presents with two hours of painless rectal bleeding, passing several large clots of bright red blood. No abdominal pain. No trauma. No NSAIDs.

PMH: diverticulosis with 2021 diverticular hemorrhage; CAD with NSTEMI (LAD stent 2024) and inferior STEMI (RCA stent 2024); Parkinson disease with psychosis; mild cognitive impairment; HTN; hyperlipidemia; BPH.
Meds: aspirin 81 (clopidogrel stopped two weeks ago), pantoprazole, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, tamsulosin, finasteride.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, former occasional alcohol. Retired teacher, lives with wife.

Triage: BP 100/60, HR 110.
Exam: pale. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Rectal: bright red blood.

Labs: Hgb 10.2 (baseline about 14), Hct 30.5, plt 250K. PT 12, INR 1.0. BUN 18, Cr 1.0.

ED course: two large-bore IVs, crystalloid with improvement in heart rate and pressure. Type and screen. With hematochezia, tachycardia and low pressure, a brisk upper GI source must be excluded before attributing this to the diverticula; GI consulted for EGD first, then colonoscopy. Aspirin held. Admitted to medicine.

Impression: hematochezia with hemodynamic instability; upper GI hemorrhage to be excluded; recurrent diverticular bleed most likely.

Emergency medicine attending

reports.text: Indication: hematochezia with tachycardia, exclude upper GI source. Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Esophagus normal. Stomach normal, no blood or coffee-ground material. Duodenal bulb and second portion normal, no blood. No ulcer, varix or vascular lesion.
reports.conclusion: Normal EGD. No upper GI bleeding source.

reports.text: Indication: recurrent hematochezia, prior diverticular bleed 2021. Prep: rapid purge, adequate. Scope advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve. Blood and clots in the sigmoid and descending colon, cleared with washing. Scattered sigmoid diverticula. One sigmoid diverticulum with an adherent clot and visible vessel at its neck; three hemostatic clips placed with hemostasis. No polyps or masses. Remainder of colon without blood after washing.
reports.conclusion: Bleeding sigmoid diverticulum, treated with clips, hemostasis. Sigmoid diverticulosis. No polyps.

2. CAD - aspirin, BB, ACEi, atorvastatin 40, PPI. Cardiology in the new year.
3. HTN - controlled.
4. Lipids, BMP today.
AWV March.

Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 01/10/2026. Received 01/13/2026.

CC: vision loss, left eye.

HPI: 72M with Parkinson disease and CAD (NSTEMI and inferior STEMI, LAD and RCA stents) with sudden painless loss of vision in the left eye about two hours before arrival, "like a curtain coming down." No eye pain, no headache, no trauma.

PMH: CAD s/p NSTEMI and inferior STEMI with stents 2024; Parkinson disease with psychosis; MCI; HTN; hyperlipidemia; BPH; diverticulosis with diverticular bleeds 2021 and 2025.
Meds: lisinopril, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, aspirin 81, pantoprazole, carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, tamsulosin, finasteride.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, former occasional alcohol, retired math teacher, lives with wife.

Vitals: BP 145/90, pulse 78 and regular.
Exam: left pupil does not react to light, left relative afferent pupillary defect. Left fundus: pale retina with a cherry-red spot at the macula. Right eye normal. No carotid bruits. Remainder of neuro exam at his baseline per wife (rest tremor right hand).

CT head without contrast: no acute intracranial abnormality.
ESR and CRP normal. CBC, BMP unremarkable. ECG sinus rhythm.

Course: ophthalmology consulted in the ED and confirmed left central retinal artery occlusion. Admitted to medicine for stroke-equivalent workup.

Impression: acute left central retinal artery occlusion.

Emergency medicine attending

reports.text: Bilateral carotid duplex. Right: common, internal and external carotid arteries with less than 50% stenosis by velocity criteria. Left: common, internal and external carotid arteries with less than 50% stenosis by velocity criteria. Antegrade vertebral flow bilaterally.
reports.conclusion: No hemodynamically significant carotid stenosis; less than 50% bilaterally.

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size. LVEF 50%. Inferior wall hypokinesis, unchanged from 6/2024. No left ventricular or left atrial thrombus seen. Valves without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 50%, known inferior hypokinesis, no intracardiac thrombus.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admission 01/10/2026 - Discharge 01/12/2026. Received 01/13/2026.

Discharge diagnosis: acute central retinal artery occlusion, left eye.

Course: 72M with CAD (LAD and RCA stents), HTN and hyperlipidemia presented with sudden painless left monocular vision loss, RAPD and a cherry-red spot. CT head without acute findings. ESR and CRP normal, making giant cell arteritis unlikely. Ophthalmology confirmed CRAO; no ocular intervention offered at this point. Workup: carotid duplex with less than 50% stenosis bilaterally; TTE LVEF 50% with the known inferior hypokinesis, no thrombus; telemetry sinus rhythm throughout. Lipids and A1c drawn. Left eye vision not improved at discharge.

Discharge medications: unchanged. Aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, pantoprazole 40, carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, rasagiline 1 mg, tamsulosin 0.4, finasteride 5, NTG prn.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: 14-day ambulatory monitor to be mailed to home. Retina clinic in 1-2 weeks. PCP within one week. Cardiology to review monitor.

Hospital medicine

Retina clinic

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Desrosiers was seen 12 days after a left central retinal artery occlusion.

Visual acuity: right eye normal; left eye count fingers.
Pupils: left relative afferent pupillary defect.
Anterior segment: no iris neovascularization either eye.
Fundus: left retinal pallor from the occlusion; no neovascularization of the disc or retina. Right fundus normal.

Assessment: left CRAO, count-fingers vision, no neovascularization.
Plan: neovascularization surveillance; return in three months or sooner for eye pain or redness. Vascular risk management per primary care and cardiology.

Retina specialist

Cardiology clinic

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Desrosiers is seen after a left central retinal artery occlusion in January, for CAD follow-up and review of the 14-day monitor. No angina. No palpitations.

Monitor: sinus rhythm throughout, no atrial fibrillation.
Recent workup: carotids less than 50% bilaterally; echo LVEF 50% with unchanged inferior hypokinesis, no thrombus.

Exam: BP and HR at goal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

Assessment: CAD with prior NSTEMI and inferior STEMI, stable. No cardiac source found for the retinal artery occlusion.
Plan: continue aspirin, metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, atorvastatin 40, pantoprazole. Return in one year.

Left eye vision has not come back. Getting used to it; more careful on stairs and curbs. Cardiology 2/9: monitor sinus throughout, no changes. No chest pain, no bleeding, no hallucinations. No falls.
Functional: independent ADLs; wife manages meds. PHQ-2 1, not depressed, "frustrated about the eye."
Advance directive reviewed, unchanged.

Exam: per flowsheet. L RAPD. Masking, R tremor. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.

Plan:
- Fall prevention reviewed with monocular vision; night lights, stair rails in place.
- CAD, HTN, HLD: continue. CMP, CBC today (lipids and A1c done in hospital in January).
- Vaccines up to date.
- RTC 3 months.
